extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communications teams, and marketers preparing press releases optimized for 2025 (mobile/AI-first distribution)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for drafting a 2025-era press release optimized for mobile, AI summarization, multimedia distribution, and social-native formats. Covers structure, lengths, required assets, metadata/schema, and distribution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-summarization-friendly structure
rubrics_metrics.description: AI summarization rules — write for LLM extraction; AI-summarization-friendly structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure content so large language models and other summarizers can extract key facts: include a tweetable one-line summary at the top, a compressed lede, clear headings, and schema/structured data. Aim for short, explicit facts and standardized fields that ease automated extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-first formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile-first format mandatory; mobile-friendly throughout (header, lede, body, contact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for single-swipe readability: short headlines (60 chars for mobile), 50-word lede, one idea per paragraph, mobile-friendly subheaders, short videos (<60 sec), clickable phone/email links, and pull-quotes positioned to appear on first scroll.

rubrics_metrics.name: Header (mobile-friendly) components
rubrics_metrics.description: Header should be mobile-friendly and include Logo; 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE' or embargo; Date and city; Headline (60 chars for mobile); Subhead (optional, expanded mobile view).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place identification and timing information at the top for quick scanning. Keep the headline to ~60 characters for mobile display; use an optional subhead that expands in mobile views for additional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede (50 words max)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lede (50 Words Max) — 5 W's compressed; mobile-readable in one swipe; tweetable one-line summary at top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compress who/what/when/where/why into a 50-word lede that can be read in a single swipe. Provide an immediate, tweetable one-line summary at the very top to aid human and AI consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body length and structure (300–500 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Body (300-500 Words) using the inverted pyramid; one idea per paragraph; mobile-friendly subheaders; embedded multimedia at relevant points; pull-quote on first scroll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the main body concise (300–500 words). Lead with the most newsworthy details, use short paragraphs each focused on a single idea, include subheaders for mobile scanning, embed multimedia where it supports the text, and surface a pull-quote early (first scroll) for visual emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes (substantive, social-ready)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes (Substantive): 25-35 words; pull-quote format for visual emphasis; attribution with title and credentials; available as standalone social asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft concise, substantive quotes of ~25–35 words that read well as pull-quotes and as standalone social copy. Always include attribution with the speaker's title/credentials and provide quote assets formatted for social use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia hub (required assets and availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia Hub: hero image (1200x630); video (under 60 sec for mobile); infographic with social dimensions; headshot library; B-roll for broadcast; all downloadable without registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a centralized multimedia hub (downloadable without registration) that contains specified assets and sizes: a hero image (1200x630), short mobile-optimized video (<60s), social-ready infographics, headshots, and broadcast B-roll. Ensure assets are clearly labeled and easy to download.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media kit (integrated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social Media Kit: tweet-length quotes; LinkedIn post drafts; Instagram-ready visuals; TikTok-ready video clips; hashtag recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a ready-to-use social kit with platform-specific copy and assets: prewritten tweet-length quotes, LinkedIn draft posts, Instagram visuals sized for the platform, short TikTok clips, and suggested hashtags to speed syndication and ensure consistent messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schema.org markup (NewsArticle + fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schema markup expected: NewsArticle type; Headline, datePublished, dateModified; Author and Organization; Image references; Multilingual versions if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish machine-readable structured data (NewsArticle schema) containing headline, datePublished/dateModified, author/organization, image URLs, and language variants where used. Proper schema supports SEO and AI extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate (concise 50–75 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate (Concise): 50-75 words including founded date, headquarters, mission in one sentence, key metrics, website URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the company boilerplate short (50–75 words). Include founding date, HQ, a one-sentence mission statement, a few key metrics, and the website URL for reporters and summarizers to reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information (mobile-friendly and actionable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact (Mobile-Friendly): named contact; direct phone (clickable on mobile); direct email (clickable); calendar booking link; time zone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List a named contact with clickable phone and email links, an optional calendar booking link for interviews, and the contact's time zone. Make reaching spokespeople as frictionless as possible on mobile devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: End marker
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude the release with the standard three-hash end marker (###) to signal completion to journalists and parsers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution requirements and strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution for 2025: Mobile-optimized HTML version; AI-readable structured data; multi-language versions; social-native formats; wire for SEO floor; direct outreach for pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute releases via a mobile-optimized HTML page with embedded schema and downloadable assets, create social-native formats, translate into target languages when appropriate, use wire services as a baseline for SEO, and conduct direct outreach to secure pickups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual / translation readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation often needed; multilingual versions recommended; schema should reference multilingual versions where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess target markets and provide multi-language releases when appropriate. Offer translated copies and mark language variants in schema to aid localized discovery and AI summarization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality checklist (modern release minimums)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric summary: Mobile-first formatting; 50-word lede; 300-500 word body; Multimedia hub; Social media kit; Schema markup; Multilingual where appropriate; AI-summarization-friendly structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist as the minimum standard for modern releases: ensure mobile-first design, concise lede and body lengths, a complete multimedia hub and social kit, proper schema, translation where needed, and overall structure optimized for AI summarizers.
